corrections.issue: Timing wrong: Andrew says hedge funds and CTAs began building the Trump trade very early in 2024, i.e. before the election, not as a post-election consensus.
corrections.fix: From early 2024 hedge funds and CTAs increasingly crowded into the 'Trump trade' (long equities, strong dollar, sticky inflation, long gold), which reversed in early 2025 and produced losses.

corrections.issue: Numbers misread: the replicator's position goes from 100 to about 80-85 (residual risk) while managers cut from 100 to about 70; '180 to 100' is a caption artefact.
corrections.fix: In sharp shocks vol controls make managers de-risk faster than a weekly replicator (e.g. managers 100 to 70, replicator 100 to about 85 at the next rebalance), but the industry never flips from fully long to fully short, so the residual lag is bounded.

corrections.issue: Speaker partly wrong: Andrew raises bank QIS as the competitive threat a decade ago; the remark that QIS performance and fees are never visible, making competition unfair, is by Niels (he explains QIS 'for those who may not know').
corrections.fix: Andrew: the main competitive threat to CTAs a decade ago was banks offering cheap QIS trend products. Niels: QIS performance and fees are not visible, so the comparison is unfair.

corrections.issue: Probable wrong speaker: this closing view follows Andrew's final thought and is answered by Niels ('Yeah, absolutely'), so it is most likely Tom Roble's final thought, not Niels's (captions have no labels).
